registered.ASSOCIATION_RULE: At each frame with detections, in order: (a) the detection that prompted a track at this frame belongs to it; (b) a detection that overlaps a track at IoU >= 0.5 belongs to that track whatever its side label (same-side track first when several qualify, then highest IoU, then lowest track ID); it never re-prompts or starts a track, and a different label is logged as a side disagreement; only a same-side detection confirms a track; (c) an unconfirmed track is re-prompted by the free same-side detection that overlaps it most at 0 < IoU < 0.5 (greedy by IoU, at most one re-prompt per track per frame); (d) an unconfirmed track whose mask has 0 pixels (lost) is re-prompted by a remaining free same-side detection, lowest track ID first; (e) any other detection starts a new track and fixes its side, unless it overlaps a track started at this frame at IoU >= 0.5. Sides apply to hand tracks (H) only; F, O and B have none. Frames are checked in order, and the clip is propagated again after the first frame where a detection re-prompts or starts a track; decisions are never undone, and tracks are never merged or deleted.
registered.BACKFILL: SAM's masks before a track's first detection (backward propagation from its first prompt) are kept, flagged per track and frame in the metadata, drawn hatched on the contact sheets, and count toward the usable-frame rule; the audit judges them.
registered.DETECTRON2_ROI_ALIGN: torchvision's roi_align kernel (torch.ops.torchvision.roi_align) for every Detectron2 ROIAlign, inference only, with a check on every Mask R-CNN and Hands23 call that it ran (density/masks/roi_align.py)
registered.HANDS23_HAND_MATCH: A Hands23 hand box joins the hand track it overlaps at IoU >= 0.5, preferring the track with the same side, then the highest IoU; a different side label is logged as a side disagreement and does not drop the observation.
registered.HAND_TRACK_CONFIRMATION: After association, a hand track is kept only if a Hands23 hand box of either side overlaps the track's mask box at IoU >= 0.5 on at least one keyframe within the track's span (the frames where the track has a mask, including those before its first detection). Unconfirmed tracks are dropped from H and never merged into another track; they stay in the metadata with the detection that started them and are outlined in grey on the contact sheets.
registered.MASK_GPU: The experiment's reference masks are computed on one GPU type: the 24 GB MIG slice of an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (RunPod Secure Cloud, US-NE-1, "NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition MIG 1g.24gb"). SAM 2.1, WiLoR, Hands23 and Mask R-CNN run on it; SCRFD stays on the onnxruntime CPU provider. The mask determinism check (T26) runs on the same GPU. Video generation runs on an H100 SXM, never on this slice.
registered.SAM_BUILD: sam-2 built with SAM2_BUILD_CUDA=0 on both machines: the _C extension is absent, so the hole-filling post-processing (fill_holes_in_mask_scores) is skipped. A CUDA build on the pod would change the masks.
registered.SAM_PRECISION: fp32 weights and activations, no autocast. SAM 2 stores memory features in bfloat16; a forward pre-hook on memory_attention casts memory and memory_pos to the dtype of the current features (fp32) on every frame, the same exact conversion PyTorch's type promotion already performs on frames with fp32 object pointers.
registered.STRATUM_REGIONS: Each reference computes only the regions its stratum uses: F for faces; H, O and C for manipulation; B for full body; nothing for controls, whose mask is the explicit empty mask.
registered.STRUCTURING_ELEMENT: Euclidean disk: pixel offsets (dx, dy) with dx^2 + dy^2 <= r^2
registered.SUSTAINED_CONTACT: Contact intervals require sustained contact: with keyframes 8 frames apart, contact shorter than 0.5 s cannot validate. The spacing is revisited only if the pilot's manipulation pass rate shows brief contacts are a common failure.

registered: Attention for generation on CUDA: FLASH_ATTENTION, then EFFICIENT_ATTENTION (density/attention.py); Session D re-measured with it.
Starting noise: generated once on CPU, saved, and always loaded from the saved file by its SHA-256, never regenerated (density/noise.py); the same seed gives different noise on x86 and ARM CPUs.

VAE convolutions: TF32, the CUDA default (density/wan.py): strict fp32 adds 13.1 to 13.2 s per video, at most 23 percent of C1's and 41 percent of C3's end-to-end time with Session B's times (18 and 33 percent with Session D's), over the 10 percent limit.

SAM 2.1 convolutions, by the same rule: strict fp32 (IEEE) (density/masks/registered.py), since strict fp32 stays within 10 percent of per-reference mask time: -1.9 percent for smoke-1 (face), +0.8 percent for smoke-2 (manipulation).
Tolerances for the four full-resolution checks: bitwise, with Session D's scope (density/tolerances.py); section 11's LPIPS check is met at zero.
The H100 canary: smoke-1's dense C1 must match pod D's latent and frame hashes at the start of every H100 session (density/canary.py).
Strict deterministic mode for the pilot and main run: a deterministic-algorithm warning stops the job (density/determinism.py).
The volume stop: du's allocated size over /workspace before each step or batch, stopping at 90 x 10^9 bytes (density/volume.py).
Detectron2's ROIAlign through torchvision's kernel for inference, checked on every call (density/masks/roi_align.py).
The mask canary: every mask model on the stock clips' first 9 frames must hash as recorded in Session F (density/mask_canary.py, configs/mask_canary.json).
attention_finding: PyTorch chose cuDNN attention on the H100 at full resolution. It is bitwise within a process, but a dense C1 rerun in a new process differs from step 0 (smoke-2 max latent diff 3.76), and it is not row-invariant. The 'all HSA groups dense' miss compared two processes, so its cause is this, not HSA. With flash attention pinned, C1 is bitwise across processes, and HSA all-full vs dense (yes) and C3's fast path vs the oracle (yes) are bitwise; the 40 dense steps took 78 s with flash against 58 s with cuDNN (wall time after loading, with a copy to the host at every step). Session D measured flash's cost with CUDA events (end to end in steady state, flash against cuDNN): C1 73.8 s against 58.1 s (+27 percent), C3 39.4 s against 32.3 s (+22 percent), C4 39.6 s against 32.3 s (+23 percent). The projections use Session D's times.
notes: On pods the CPU pools run at the cgroup quota rounded down, with one inter-op thread (density/cpu_threads.py, scripts/pod/env.sh). Chase approved it on 2026-10-07; it is not a registered value, since no output changed on the slice.
Deterministic mode fills newly allocated memory (torch.utils.deterministic.fill_uninitialized_memory), which costs a little time in every run; the timings include it.

flash-compare.label: flash in a new process vs the saved flash run

mask_roi_align.note: mask_threads.py found Mask R-CNN and Hands23 spending about 20 s an image in one compiled region. With deterministic algorithms on and the input on CUDA, torchvision 0.29.1 replaces its roi_align kernel with a pure-Python version, lazily torch.compile'd, which exists to make the backward pass deterministic (torchvision/ops/roi_align.py). The masks need only the forward pass, and the kernel's forward pass computes each output on one thread, without atomics.
